sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an organized card-not-present fraud scheme involving customer C01727 and primary card C01727-K2, connected to an ongoing attack pattern impacting 16 other customer cards. Between January 17, 2017, and January 28, 2017, three unauthorized online transactions totaling $967.68 were executed on card C01727-K2. The unauthorized charges include transaction 3660261 for $305.41 on January 17, 2017, transaction 3660262 for $366.35 on January 18, 2017, and transaction 3660263 for $295.92 on January 28, 2017. All three purchases were conducted online within region 231 for product-C, listing payer email addresses at gmail.com and recipient email addresses at sc.rr.com. No device telemetry, persistent device identifiers, or proxy indicators were captured during the authorization attempts. This activity represents an abrupt departure from the cardholder's baseline of strictly in-person product-W transactions in region 231. Furthermore, legitimate in-person transactions continued locally during this same timeframe, including transactions 3607094 and 3607101, confirming that physical custody of the card was retained while card details were exploited remotely. Knowledge graph analysis identified that 16 other cards, including C05610-K1, C01594-K1, and C03060-K1, similarly transacted with recipient domain sc.rr.com over the prior 30 days, compared to zero in the preceding two months. Card C01727-K2 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases, demonstrating repeat exposure to compromise. The bank has blocked card C01727-K2, initiated monitoring on all 16 connected cards, and filed this report to document the coordinated fraud ring.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

report.sar_narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details an organized card-not-present fraud scheme involving customer C01727 and primary card C01727-K2, connected to an ongoing attack pattern impacting 16 other customer cards. Between January 17, 2017, and January 28, 2017, three unauthorized online transactions totaling $967.68 were executed on card C01727-K2. The unauthorized charges include transaction 3660261 for $305.41 on January 17, 2017, transaction 3660262 for $366.35 on January 18, 2017, and transaction 3660263 for $295.92 on January 28, 2017. All three purchases were conducted online within region 231 for product-C, listing payer email addresses at gmail.com and recipient email addresses at sc.rr.com. No device telemetry, persistent device identifiers, or proxy indicators were captured during the authorization attempts. This activity represents an abrupt departure from the cardholder's baseline of strictly in-person product-W transactions in region 231. Furthermore, legitimate in-person transactions continued locally during this same timeframe, including transactions 3607094 and 3607101, confirming that physical custody of the card was retained while card details were exploited remotely. Knowledge graph analysis identified that 16 other cards, including C05610-K1, C01594-K1, and C03060-K1, similarly transacted with recipient domain sc.rr.com over the prior 30 days, compared to zero in the preceding two months. Card C01727-K2 also has five prior confirmed fraud cases, demonstrating repeat exposure to compromise. The bank has blocked card C01727-K2, initiated monitoring on all 16 connected cards, and filed this report to document the coordinated fraud ring.
